description:
## Context

Scenarios that expose LLM-callable tools today (agent-manager, scenario-to-cloud) hand-write ~100 lines of protobuf ToolDefinition boilerplate per tool. Canonical schema lives at `packages/proto/schemas/agent-inbox/v1/domain/tool.proto`. This research defines the authoring ergonomics so adding a tool collapses to ~10 lines and every scenario follows the same pattern.

## Research Goals

1. **Toolkit shape**: codegen from proto vs. hand-written Go builder helpers vs. hybrid. Prototype both on a representative existing tool (e.g., `spawn_coding_agent` in agent-manager). Compare line count, IDE experience, type safety, maintenance cost.
2. **Package home**: extend `packages/api-core` vs. a new `packages/tool-core` vs. a subdir of an existing package. Default is extend existing; reconsider only if research surfaces a clean boundary.
3. **Canonical scenario location**: `api/tools/` directory with one file per tool vs. grouped by category. Decide the convention that the authoring skill and template will lock.
4. **Manifest composition**: how a scenario's tool files compose into the runtime `/api/v1/tools` response.
5. **Migration cost**: how existing hand-written tool implementations in agent-manager and scenario-to-cloud convert — this is dogfood.

## Deliverables

- Toolkit design with a worked example of a real tool before/after
- Package-home decision with rationale
- Canonical file layout spec
- Migration plan sketch for agent-manager + scenario-to-cloud
- Boilerplate line-count target

## Out of Scope

- Scenario-auditor rule design (separate execute item)
- Prompt-manager skills (separate execute item)
- Template scaffolding (separate execute item)
- Anything agent-inbox-side (unified retrieval initiative)

title: Design the shared Go toolkit for proto-tool authoring
